Question
========
An organizational psychology study investigates whether a team-building program 
increases employees' work engagement. A total of ($N=`r N`$) employees participate 
in a six-week intervention. Work engagement is measured before and after the intervention 
using the Utrecht Work Engagement Scale (UWES-9; from 0 = lowest to 6 = highest work engagement).
The significance level is set to ($\alpha=.05$), two-tailed.

````{r, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(tab, caption="_Table 1._ UWES-9 scores at T0, EOT, and D=EOT−T0.")
````
Does the team-building program lead to a meaningful difference (i.e., more than $\mu_0=`r mu_0`$ units) in work engagement? 
Please report the $t$-ratio.

```{r questionlist, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
answerlist(t$alternatives, markup="markdown")
```

Solution
========
The $t$-statistic for paired samples is given by $t=\frac{\overline{D}-\mu_0}{s_D / \sqrt{N}}$. 

```{r solutionlist, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
answerlist(sol, markup="markdown")
```
